One event coded to Liria village, Juba county, Central Equatoria state. A child abduction on 22 July 2023 in the same area has been coded separately.

On 22 July 2023, an unknown group abducted a young boy in the area of Opiri/Ofiri in Liria payam (Juba county, Central Equatoria state), and wounded the mother of the child during a scuffle, causing minor injuries.

On 21 July 2023, an unknown group killed a man and abducted his wife and four children (two girls, and two boys) at an unspecified location in Duk county (Jonglei state, location coded to admin2 HQ of Duk Padiet) as they were travelling to Fangak county.

notes: On 26 July 2023, a mob lynched an NSS operative in Chukudum town (Budi county, Eastern Equatoria state), after an incident in which a person was killed at their home the same day (coded separately). On 19 July 2023, a group of school pupils attacked a man at Maper East Primary School (located at an unspecified location within Nyalath payam, Aweil Centre county, Northern Bahr el Ghazal state), after he physically assaulted a teacher at the school for excessively disciplining his child. Teachers intervened to protect the man from the children (who also damaged his motorbike) until police arrived.

On 4 July 2018, unknown gunmen attacked armed youth in Eastern Lakes state (no location specified, coordinates for Yirol used). 19 were reported killed (two attackers, ten armed youth, three children and four women), and 11 injured. The source suggests this was a cattle raid, though the Eastern Lakes state minister for information implied SPLM-IO involvement (the SPLM-IO has not yet responded to the claim).

On December 1st and/or December 2nd, two armed Nyang Dinka sub-clans (the Kwac-thiin and Kwac-diit ) clashed at Kwacdiit (coordinates for Yirol, Lakes state, used), leaving four dead and seventeen wounded. The dispute appears to centre upon a grazing area.

On 27 January 2019, two Ciec Dinka sub-clans clashed in the area of Majak-Jok (coordinates for Yirol, Lakes state, used). The Kuac-Dit clan were reported to have attacked the Kuac-Thii, as part of a series of attacks beginning November 2018. One Kuac-Dit fighter was killed.
On Jan 12th, unknown gunmen attacked a civilian vehicle at an unspecified location in Yirol West (Lakes state, coordinates for Yirol used at precision 2), injuring two passengers.

On 9 May 2019, 21 nurses at the civil hospital in Yirol (Lakes state) demonstrated against a 75% pay cut, due to the withdrawal of funding by an NGO supporting health care costs at the hospital. The nurses reportedly attacked foreign nurses who were not striking, though the report does not mention the number of injured. Police arrested the nurses, before releasing them pending trial two days later.

On or before August 12th, unidentified attackers killed 13 civilians (including a child) and wounded 7, at an unspecified location in the disputed Eastern Lakes state (Lakes state, coordinates for Yirol used at prec3). The assailants looted cattle.
22 September. In Yirol, 11 people were killed and 14 wounded in South Sudan on Sunday during tribal clashes over a contested land between the Nuer and Dinka clans.

As reported on 17 December 2019, hundreds of pro-government protesters delivered a petition to the Governor of the disputed Eastern Lakes state (the location is presumed to be Yirol, Lakes state, and has been coded as such at geoprec1), calling for the controversial 32 states system to remain.
On 14 February 2020, pro-government protests took place in Yirol (Lakes state), calling for the controversial 32 states system to be maintained.

On 7 June 2020, two groups of armed youth from Aluak-luak and Amoli cattle camps in the Yirol area (Lakes state) clashed, killing at least 2 and wounding 4, with several children also suspected of being abducted. The attack is described as retaliatory in nature.

Around 15 July 2020 (month of), four civilians were killed by an unknown group as they travelled along the Kapoeta-Ngauro (a.k.a. Lauro) road of Eastern Equatoria state. The killings come amid tension between the Didinga and Toposa communities.

On 4 October 2020, a soldier threw two grenades at mourners attending the funeral of the late ambassador to Kuwait in Yirol town (Lakes state), wounding 8 (2 or 3 seriously). The soldier has been arrested, though the motive is unclear.

Around 27 February 2021 (weekend of), 'cattle-related violence' took place at an unspecified location in the Yirol area (Lakes state), presumed to be in Yirol West county given recent violence in the area. At least 5 people were killed between this event and another in Cueibet county (fatalities distributed across two events), and there is no mention of the identity of the attackers, nor whether an exchange of fire took place.

On 2 March 2021, the Aper and Pankuolin groups of Yirol West (presumed to be sub-sections of Atuot sections) clashed at an unspecified location in Yirol West county (Lakes state), killing 4 and wounding 4. A local official has described the incident as being linked to a revenge killing.

On 29 January 2023, a prominent chief from Yirol East was arrested in Pagarau payam and then transferred to Maburzeet detention facility in Yirol town (Yirol West county, Lakes state), where he was tortured and seriously wounded by SSPDF soldiers, four of whom were later arrested. The chief had been felling mahogany trees for the construction of his home, which is believed to be the cause of the initial arrest.

On 10 April 2023, a local SPLM party secretary was beaten with a stick by a police officer in Yirol market (Yirol West county, Lakes state), after he intervened in a dispute between police and a market vendor (who may also have been beaten by police).

On 23 July 2023, militia (described as coming from Duk county, and presumed to be Hol and/or Nyarweng Dinka, coded as Dinka, operating alongside militia from the Yuai area and/or Ayod county, and presumed to be Lou and/or Gawaar Nuer, coded as Nuer) clashed with local militia (presumed to be Murle) at Rang village in the area of Nanaam (Pibor county, Jonglei state). An unknown number of people were killed in the fighting (unknown fatalities coded as 3).

On 25 July 2023, militia (described as coming from Duk county, and presumed to be Hol and/or Nyarweng Dinka, coded as DInka, operating alongside militia from the Yuai area and/or Ayod county, and presumed to be Lou and/or Gawaar Nuer, coded as Nuer) clashed with local militia (presumed to be Murle) in the Nanaam area (Pibor county, Jonglei state). An unknown number of people were killed in the fighting (unknown fatalities coded as 3).

Around 1 August 2023 (between 31 July - 2 August), a local group, coded as communal militia, killed two women and wounded a child in Kapoeta town (Kapoeta South county, Eastern Equatoria state), in what is believed to be a revenge attack for an incident on 29 July (coded separately). One of the women was heavily pregnant, and the child was removed from her womb after she was pronounced dead at hospital. The new-born infant then died one hour later.

Around 27 July 2023, cattle raiders from Rumbek East county (presumed to be Agar Dinka) stole 16 cows and abducted a boy at an unspecified location in Yirol West county (Lakes state; location presumed to be near to the border with Rumbek East, and is coded to Aluak-Luak town). The boy was later released, and the cattle subsequently recovered during a clash with security forces (coded separately).

On 27 July 2023, security forces (described as being 'the armed forces', and coded as SSPDF) clashed with cattle raiders from Panawac boma (presumed to be Agar Dinka) at an unspecified location in Atiaba payam (Rumbek East county, Lakes state), killing the leader of the cattle raiders. 16 head of cattle that had been stolen in Yirol West were returned to their owners.

Around 5 July 2023 (week of), clashes between unidentified communal militias were reported at a newly discovered mining site implied to be near to Lowereng village (phonetic spelling used) in Kapoeta North county (Eastern Equatoria state. No location with the same or similar name found, and the event has been coded to the admin2 HQ of Riwoto). Casualties unknown.

On 9 July 2023, at least 10 people were killed and three others wounded in Lowereng village (phonetic spelling used) in Kapoeta North county (Eastern Equatoria state. No location with the same or similar name found, and the event has been coded to the admin2 HQ of Riwoto). The incident follows clashes over a newly discovered mining site in the previous week. Event presumed to be an armed clash between unidentified communal militias pending further information.

On 1 August 2023, attackers (suspected of coming from the Greater Pibor Administrative Area, and presumed to be Murle) killed four people and wounded four others at an unspecified location in Uleng boma (described as being 8km south of Yuai, and coded to Akar, Uror county, Jonglei state). 100 head of cattle were also stolen. Victims presumed to be Lou Nuer.

On 29 July 2023, an unknown local group, coded as communal militia, killed at least three people at an unspecified location along the Torit-Kapoeta road (implied to be in the Greater Kapoeta area, and coded to Morugurn, Kapoeta South county, Eastern Equatoria state). The source indicates the violence is related to recent fighting between unspecified local groups in Kapoeta North (coded separately).

Around 1 August 2023 (between 1 August - 2 August), a mob severely beat a man in Kapoeta town (Kapoeta South county, Eastern Equatoria state), with the victim being accused of involvement in the recent killing of two women in the town (coded separately). Authorities rescued the man, who died of his injuries in hospital, and noted that the victim was not among their suspects for the recent killings.

Around 13 October 2018 (weekend of), further clashes took place between the Kobura and Nyangwara clans of the Mundari ethnic group at an unspecified location in Terekeka county (Central Equatoria, location coded to admin2 HQ of Terekeka town). 22 people in total were killed in clashes (5 fatalities coded for this event, with 17 coded to two events from the previous week). Estimates for injuries vary, with higher estimates at between 30 and 36.

On 10 November 2022, armed individuals killed six people whilst traveling between the Kilo 10 and Kilo 20 areas of Melut county (Upper Nile state; coded to Kilo 20), amid violence between Mabanese and Nyiel Dinka militias. It is unclear who the victims and attackers were in the ambush.

Around 2 August 2023 (as reported), fighting continued between a militia (described as coming from Duk county, and presumed to be Hol and/or Nyarweng Dinka, coded as Dinka, operating alongside militia from the Yuai area and/or Ayod county, and presumed to be Lou and/or Gawaar Nuer, coded as Nuer) with local militia (presumed to be Murle) at an unspecified location(s) in Pibor county (Jonglei state; event coded to Nanaam given recent fighting in the same area). Authorities have stated there were two casualties (with no details provided regarding the extent of the injuries), though say the remoteness of the area means information is severely limited.

Around 15 June 2023 (month of), an individual (described as being a 'young man' and a 'boy') was abducted by an unspecified armed group at an unspecified location in Yei county (Central Equatoria state), and forced to undertake military training with the group. The victim later escaped from the group in August 2023.

On 12 August 2023, armed youth (suspected of being from the Greater Pibor Administrative Area, and presumed to be Murle) ambushed a boda boda (motorbike taxi) rider and a woman at an unspecified location, implied to be in south-western Jonglei state (location coded to Twic East admin2 HQ of Panyagor). The women was robbed and then abducted, but was able to escape. Victims presumed to be Dinka. Authorities in Pibor have stated that they do not have information regarding the incident, and have pledged to investigate.

On 12 August 2023, attackers (suspected of being from the Greater Pibor Administrative Area, and presumed to be Murle) abducted three women and one man (presumed to be Dinka) in the area of Wernyol (Twic East county, Jonglei state). The male abductee escaped his captors.

Around 29 August 2023 (as reported), a group of SSPDF soldiers stole household items and solar panels from a pastor in Yei (Yei county, Central Equatoria state), and forced three youths to carry equipment for them. The soldiers had spent the night at the pastor's house after becoming lost. At least two officers (one source says 12 soldiers) were arrested, and the stolen items were returned.

On 14 August 2023, police clashed with armed men (presumed to be Bul Nuer) at an unspecified location in Wang Kei payam (Mayom county, Unity state), wounding one of the armed men. Three armed men were arrested, and are believed to have been involved in a previous incident (for which no date is provided) in which local administrators in the area were attacked (and an elder was killed).

On 27 August 2023, cattle raiders from Panyijiar county (presumed to be Nyong or Dor Nuer) ambushed armed pastoralists from Yirol East (presumed to be Ciec Dinka) at an unspecified location in Adior payam (Yirol East county, Lakes state), killing two. The cattle raiders had earlier raided an unspecified number of cattle from the pastoralists. Two people were also wounded between this event and another in the Nyang area (coded separately).

On 24 July 2023, unspecified attackers ambushed a vehicle at an unspecified location between Gumuruk and Pibor town in Pibor county (Jonglei state; location coded to Beh). An aid worker was beaten and wounded during the incident.

On 29 July 2023, SSPDF soldiers shot and killed a civilian (presumed to be Bari) at Nyarabanga village in Kit boma (location coded to Kit, Juba county, Central Equatoria state). There is no further information.

Around 11 August 2023 (as reported), an unknown armed group shot dead a man (presumed to be Dinka) as he travelled at an unspecified location in Duk county (Jonglei state, location coded to admin2 HQ of Duk Padiet). There is no further information.

On 12 August 2023, armed youth (suspected of being from the Greater Pibor Administrative Area, and presumed to be Murle) ambushed a tractor carrying four Sudanese traders at an unspecified location between Bor town and Panyagor (location coded to Jalle, Bor South county, Jonglei state). One of the traders was killed, and the other three robbed. Authorities in Pibor have stated that they do not have information regarding the attack, and have pledged to investigate.

Around 13 August 2023 (between 29 July - 31 August), SSPDF soldiers were reported to have attempted to assassinate a chief of Karpeto boma at an unspecified location (presumed to be at or near to Karpeto, Juba county, Central Equatoria state), before looting the house of the chief. The source does not specify whether the victim was wounded in the attempt on his life. Victim presumed to be Bari.

On 14 August 2023, attackers (suspected of being from the Greater Pibor Administrative Area, and presumed to be Murle) ambushed a group travelling at an unspecified location between Wernyol and Panyagor (location coded to Kiirbeer, Twic East county, Jonglei state), killing two people, with a third person reported to be missing. Victims presumed to be Dinka. Authorities in Pibor have stated that they do not have information regarding the incident, and have pledged to investigate.

On 16 August 2023, police were reported to have beaten a student in custody in Wau (Wau county, Western Bahr el Ghazal state), after they arrested the student during demonstrations at the University of Bahr el Ghazal the same day (coded separately). Note that the student was not involved in the demonstration, but had been arrested after ignoring directives from security forces deployed to the campus.

On 19 August 2023, unknown attackers shot and wounded a child in the leg in the Haforiere area (Torit county, Eastern Equatoria state). The local paramount chief has alleged the attackers were rustlers from the Boya ethnic group, though has also claimed the attackers tracks ran to the Lobira area of Ikotos county (a non-Boya area). The county commissioner has attributed the attack to youth from both Budi and Ikotos counties. Victim presumed to be Lotuko.

On 19 August 2023, unknown attackers killed a man who was herding goats in the Hiyala area (Torit county, Eastern Equatoria state). The local paramount chief has alleged the attackers were rustlers from the Boya ethnic group of Budi county, though has also claimed the attackers tracks ran to the Lobira area of Ikotos county (a non-Boya area). The county commissioner has attributed the attack to youth from both Budi and Ikotos counties. Victim presumed to be Lotuko.

On 23 August 2023, an unknown group killed a trader after abducting him at Ombasi (Yei county, Central Equatoria state), and stole three motorbikes. Authorities say the victim had previously been abducted from Yei town before being released, and have suggested the incident may relate to forcible recruitment. One source says the attackers were NAS forces, though this is unconfirmed.

On 23 August 2023, attackers (suspected of being Nuer from Mayom county who had relocated to neighboring Twic county, and presumed to be Bul Nuer) killed three people in two separate attacks on the same day (one event coded) in 'Kerie payam' in Mayom county (Unity state; note no payam exists with that name, and the location is coded to Keriel near the border with Twic county), with two of the victims being women. The victims (all presumed to be Bul Nuer) are relatives of a spiritual leader, who the attackers allegedly threatened prior to the attack, accusing him of being ethnic Dinka rather than an ethnic Nuer.

On 23 August 2023, seven traders (implied to come from Mayom county, and presumed to be Bul Nuer) were killed by an unidentified group at an unspecified location in Tonj North county (location coded to Madul, Tonj North county, Warrap state, on the assumption the event took place near to the common border between Mayom and Tonj North). The motive for the attack is not specified.

On 23 August 2023, a cattle trader (implied to come from Mayom county, and presumed to be Bul Nuer) was killed at an unspecified location in Tonj North county after crossing into the county (location coded to Madul, Tonj North county, Warrap state, on the assumption the event took place near to the common border between Mayom and Tonj North). The motive for the attack is not specified.

On 25 August 2023, SSPDF soldiers were reported to have attacked and looted 'Christian believers' residents who had recently returned to South Sudan from Uganda at Monga village (Yei county, Central Equatoria state), and stolen the clerical attire of a reverend from the Monga/Mongo parish of the Episcopal Church. Injuries not reported.

On 29 August 2023, a member of the SSPDF, deployed to the Luwalla SSPDF Military Barracks, shot and injured a local head chief around Luwala (Juba County, Central Equatoria). According to media reports, the soldier came to the home of the chief earlier in the day to ask for a cigarette and the chief offered him money before he left. The soldier returned for the second time to ask for food, but when he was told that there was no food left, he shot the victim twice in the chest. The latter is reportedly receiving medical attention at a health facility in Juba.

Recruitment: Around 21 August 2023 (as reported), the SSPDF were alleged to have forcefully recruited at least 176 youths in Mayom county (Unity state), who were taken for training at an unspecified location in Riak payam. The source claims local chiefs were required to produce youth for training or face fines, and further alleges that soldiers linked to Maj. Gen. Matthew Puljang (a prominent commander who was removed from Mayom county in 2020) are being removed from their positions.

Weapons seizure: Around 27 July 2023 (between 9 July - 15 August), SSPDF collected around 4,000 small arms (including light machine guns) from unspecified location in Terekeka county (location coded to admin2 HQ of Terekeka town, Terekeka county, Central Equatoria state), following a series of incidents involving armed Mundari pastoralists. The weapons are here presumed to have been largely gathered from members of the Mundari group.

Looting: Around 30 August 2023 (as reported), South Sudanese returnees fleeing the conflict in Sudan were robbed by armed youth as they traveled from Bentiu to Guit in Unity state (location implied to be in Guit county, and is coded to the admin 2 HQ of Guit town). Two people have been arrested and tried in relation to the incident. Victims and perpetrators presumed to be Western Jikany Nuer.
On 15 August 2023, students demonstrated at the University of Bahr el Ghazal in Wau town (Wau county, Western Bahr el Ghazal state), denouncing a substantial increase in tuition fees.

On 16 August 2023, students once again demonstrated at the University of Bahr el Ghazal in Wau town (Wau county, Western Bahr el Ghazal state), denouncing a substantial increase in tuition fees. A university official has alleged that the students 'blockaded the main administration area' and prevented staff from leaving, though there is no mention of the means through the alleged blockade occurred.
Around 13 August 2023 (between 29 July - 31 August), SSPDF soldiers were reported to have raped a woman in the Karpeto area (Juba county, Central Equatoria state). Victim presumed to be Bari.
Around 13 August 2023 (between 29 July - 31 August), SSPDF soldiers were reported to have raped a woman in the Luwala area (Juba county, Central Equatoria state). Victim presumed to be Bari.

Early March 2018, Pagok Clan Militia attacked Pathiong clan members at an unknown location in Lakes state. One person from the Pathiong clan was killed.

On 23 March 2018, Pathiong clan attacked Pagok clan members in Abyei Ajok, Lakes state in retaliation for the killing of one their members at the beginning of March 2018. Four people from the Pagok clan were killed.

On 4 August 2018, a fight between youths from the Athok (assumed to be an alternate spelling of the Athoc section of the Bor Dinka) and Awan section (presumed to be a section of the Twic East Dinka clan) resulted in one person being shot dead, and two being injured. The clash took place in Wun-Lir in the disputed Twic South county [coded to Kongor town, Twic East county, Jonglei state] prior to a wrestling match. Several people were arrested.

On 18 March 2019, Ciec Dinka clashed with members of the Ajuong section of the Twic East Dinka at an unspecified location in the disputed Malek county in Yirol East county (Lakes state) [coded to Malek]. The clashes are part of a dispute over the ownership of the Liet-Buoi swamp. Two militiamen died (one from each side), and five Ajuong Dinka were wounded. Police intervened, and established a larger presence in the area.

On 23 March 2019, unknown gunmen attacked a commercial vehicle on the road between Rumbek and Tonj, approximately 20 km outside of Tonj (Warrap state, coordinates for Wun Shol used at precision 2). A soldier (assumed to be guarding the truck) was killed in the attack, and the truck (which was operated by a Somali) was looted.

At an unspecified time (though likely to be in late March or early April, and coded as April first at timeprec3) a clash (or clashes) occurred between militias from Manyangok and Wahn Alel counties (both actors coded as Tonj militia) killing 9 and wounding 22. The clashes were related to disputes on grazing and farmland areas. One event coded in Wun Shol in Mayangok county (Warrap state) at geoprec2.

During the month of October 2019, armed fishers attacked Chuei-akuet (Lakes state, coordinates for Adundit used at geoprec2), clashing with Ciec and/or Ajuong Dinka clans in the area (both actors coded). The sources makes no mention of deaths or injuries. One event coded at time prec3.

On 8 March 2020, a truck carrying an SSPDF soldier, a Kenyan truck driver and a co-driver of unspecified nationality was attacked by unknown gunmen at Makuei on the Cuiebet-Tonj road in Tonj South county (Warrap state). The attackers killed the driver, but fled once the soldier returned fire.

On 15 May 2020, Jur Bel and members of the Ayiel section of the Gok Dinka clan clashed at an unspecified location of Ngap payam in Cueibet county (Lakes state), killing at least four. The clash is said to be a revenge attack.

On 17 June 2020, suspected Murle raiders clashed with local youths (including the Alian subsection of the Athoc section of the Bor Dinka clan, and other unspecified Athoc subsections) at Aliang in Bor South county (Jonglei state), with Bor youth repulsing the attackers and recovering cattle stolen during the clash. Five were killed and seven wounded.

On 31 August 2020, a police officer was killed in Cueibet town (Lakes state) in what are described as a series revenge killings between among Gok Dinka sections (with the Kongor sub-sub-section of the Panyar sub-section of the Macar section and the Waat subsection of the Macar section presented as being the attackers, against members of the Ayiel subsection of the Langdiing section).

On 31 August 2020, two men riding on boda bodas were killed close to Cueibet town (Lakes state) in what are described as a series revenge killings between among Gok Dinka sections (with the Kongor sub-sub-section of the Panyar sub-section of the Macar section and the Waat subsection of the Macar section presented as being the attackers, against members of the Ayiel subsection of the Langdiing section).

On 24 September 2020, armed raiders from the Ayiel subsection of the Langdiing section of the Gok Dinka killed a woman from the Pagok subsection of the Langdiing during a livestock raid at Guaru cattle camp near Agngrial in Cueibet county (Lakes state).

On 25 September 2020, armed pastoralists from the Pagok and Ayiel subsections of the Langdiing section of the Gok Dinka clashed in the area of Agngrial in Cueibet county (Lakes state), after the killing of a woman the previous day. At least 10 (one source says 11) are reported to have been killed (some of whom died later of their injuries), with civilians among the dead.

On 28 September 2020, armed pastoralists from the Pagok and Ayiel subsections of the Langdiing section of the Gok Dinka clashed once again in the area of Agngrial in Cueibet county (Lakes state), with two reported to be seriously wounded.

On 8 December 2020, the director of prisons for Cueibet county (who was off-duty at the time) was killed in Mayath (Cueibet, Lakes) by suspected members of the Joth sub section of the Langdiing section of the Gok Dinka clan, in what is described as a revenge attack. The victim was a member of the Waat sub section of the Macar section of the Gok.

On 9 December 2020, fighting broke out among Gok Dinka clans in Mayath in Cueibet county (Lakes state), following the killing of the county prison director the previous day. The fighting involved members of the Joth and Ayiel sub-sections of the Langdiing section, and members of the Waat and Kongor subsections of the Macar section. Military forces are reported to have joined the fighting, and split along clan lines. 15 have been killed and at least 17 wounded (some seriously), whilst houses were torched and hundreds displaced.

On 30 December 2020, attackers from Pagor and Duony payams (and presumed to be members of the Waat sub-section of the Macar section the Gok Dinka, and from the Pagok sub-sub-section of the Pagok sub-section of the Langdiing of the Gok clan) killed a sub-chief from the Jur Bel in Agngrial in Cueibet county (Lakes state). 56 head of cattle were also stolen, 26 of which have been recovered.

On 9 January 2021, suspected Murle raiders attacked a mother and her three children who had been displaced due to flooding from north-west Bor county (all victims presumed to be of the Athoc section of the Bor Dinka) in the area of Char Akau in Bor South county (Jonglei state). An eight-month old girl was killed in the attack and two boys abducted; the mother was released unharmed.

On 15 January 2021, a child from Ayiel sub-section of the Langdiing section of the Gok Dinka was killed at Alel village close to Cueibet town (Lakes state), in what is described as a revenge killing, presumed to have been perpetrated by a Gok Dinka militia.

On 7 February 2021, a civilian (who was a member of the Joth sub-section of the Langdiing section of the Gok Dinka) was shot by an unknown group at his home in Mayath payam (Cueibet county, Lakes state). The attackers are implied to be from another Gok Dinka section, amid continued inter-sectional killings and attacks in the area.

On 11 March 2021, members of the Pagok sub-section of the Langdiing section of the Gok Dinka shot and killed an SSPDF soldier at an unspecified cattle camp in Ayiel territory in central Cueibet county (Lakes state) [coded to Kunyuk]. There is no clear motive at this time.

On 11 March 2021, members of the Ayiel sub-section of the Langdiing section of the Gok Dinka attacked members of the Pagok sub-section in retaliation for the killing of an SSPDF soldier earlier that day. The two groups clashed at an unspecified area in Cueibet county (Lakes state), presumed to be close to the incident from the same day [coded to Kunyuk]. 10 were killed in the fighting.

On 13 May 2021, militia from the Pagok subsection of the Langdiing section of the Gok Dinka attacked members of the Ayiel subsection at Aciminti village (Cueibet county, Lakes state), in retaliation for the earlier killing of a prison officer. 5 were killed 15 wounded. The sources do not state that a firefight took place, and all casualties are therefore assumed to be from the Ayiel subsection.

Around 6 April 2022 (as reported), cattle raiders from Rumbek North county (presumed to be of the Pakam section of the Agar Dinka) clashed with militia from the Waat and Kongor subsections of the Macar section of the Gok Dinka alongside members of the Pagok subsection of the Langdiing section of the Gok Dinka at an unspecified location of Cueibet county (Lakes state; location is implied to be in Abiriu payam, and has been coded as such). actor1: SPLM-In Opposition: Sudan People's Liberation Movement-In Opposition

On 19 November 2023, armed young people from the Logir community attacked and clashed with members of the Buya community in Faraksika Boma (Budi, Eastern Equatoria) during an attempt to raid cattle. 1 Buya man was killed.

On 20 November 2023, suspected members of the Murle community raided around 16 cattle and clashed with local people (likely Duk Pajut communal militia, who live in the area) when they tried to retrieve the raided cattle in Pajut Boma (Duk, Jonglei). There were no casualties.

On 20 November 2023, suspected armed young people from the Aguok section of the Rek Dinka community shot and killed an old man from the Kuac section of the Rek Dinka community in Juet village under Alek South Payam (coded as Alek, Gogrial West, Warrap). On 21 November 2023, unidentified armed men, suspected to be from the Murle community, kidnapped three children in Pak Village (Nyirol, Jonglei). Motivation of the abduction unknown/not reported. Victims are likely from the Lou Nuer community, who are predominant in the area.

On 21 November 2023, an armed young person suspected to be from the Aguok section of the Rek Dinka community shot and killed two people from the Kuac section of the Rek Dinka community in Ajiep area (Gogrial West, Warrap). On 22 November 2023, armed young people from the Twic Dinka community were suspected to have attacked three people in Tong Liet area (Twic, Warrap). Two people were killed. Motivation of the attack unknown/not reported.

On 27 August 2024, unidentified age-set members (likely from the Murle community based on incident location) clashed in Kongor area of Likuangole Payam (Pibor, Jonglei), resulting in 1 injury. Motivation unknown/not reported.

On 13 September 2024, suspected members of NAS militants shot and wounded three civilians in Wonduruba payam (Juba, Central Equatoria) for unknown or unreported reasons.

On 28 August 2023, armed members of the Ciec Clan of the Dinka (likely members of the Lou-Kuacthii Ciec Sub-Clan pf the Dinka) shot and killed a female from the Nuer (likely from the Dor Clan of the Nuer) in a suspected revenge attack in Nyang (Yirol East County, Lakes State). The motives of the attack were not specified.

On 29 August 2023, two groups of IDPs armed with knives and sticks reportedly fought at the Malakal PoC in the Malakal UNMISS Protection of Civilians site (Malakal County, Upper Nile State). 3 people sustained injuries. Later reports indicated that members of the Community Watch Group at the Malakal PoC arrested and detained 1 person in connection with the incident.

On 29 August 2023, an armed individual from the Nyei Section of the Ciec Clan from the Dinka shot and killed a member of the Duorbar Section of the Ciec Clan of the Dinka at the Mamer Cattle Camp in Adior Payam (Yirol East County, Lakes State). Local sources indicated that the victim was killed during an attempt to steal cows from the perpetrator.

On 29 August 2023, an IDP attempted to physically assault a UNPOL officer in the Malakal UNMISS Protection of Civilians site (Malakal County Upper Nile State). According to reports, other UNPOL officers intervened, arrested and detained the culprit. The motives of the perpetrator remained unclear at the time of reporting.

On 29 August 2023, members of the Kurenen Clan of the Murle reportedly clashed internally at the Jebel Boma Market in Boma (Pibor County, Jonglei State). 1 member of the Kurenen Clan was killed during the incident.

On 30 August 2023, alleged members of the SSPDF reportedly shot and killed a local businessman and local chief along the Yambio-Gangura Road near Gangura (Yambio County, Western Equatoria State). The businessman was riding a motorcycle to his garden when the assailants shot him and burnt his body together with the motorcycle. The motive for the killing remained unclear. 2 members of the SSPDF have been arrested and detained in connection with the incident.

Looting: On 30 August 2023, suspected armed members of the Agar Clan of the Dinka from Rumbek Center County raided an unspecified number of cows from members of the Langdiing-Pathiang-Gok Sub-Clan of the Dinka at the Kuer-cum grazing land in Majook Cattle Cam near Abiriu (Cueibet County, Lakes State).
